events.finding: Duration produced a strong shortcut baseline and was not accepted as the intended acoustic solution.
Direct conditional deletion classification did not meet the required signal.
Scalar R3 evidence largely captured mismatch rather than deletion.
Temporal evidence showed moderate deletion-related information.
MFA could not provide a fixed interval for a phone that was deleted.
Deterministic sliding-logit DP strongly suppressed DELETE.
A global prior scale could not rescue the deterministic DP family.
Self-trained word-level CTC was technically feasible.
CNN-only CTC learned sequences but under-generated and produced weak deletion decisions.
Both under-generation and broad phone confusion contributed.
One BiGRU materially improved phone-sequence modeling, but deletion confirmation gates still failed.
TRAIN-only continuous CTC hypothesis scores strongly separated deletion.
The frozen RAW TRAIN threshold transferred poorly despite strong continuous validation signal.
TRAIN-speaker LOSO selected TARGET normalization and a robust median threshold.
The final iterative development validation passed only 3 of 8 frozen gates.
The R4 deletion branch is closed without TEST access.
